paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches: blessings are meant to point us back to the LORD, not away from Him. Israel was a luxuriant vine, and the better the land produced, the better they made their sacred pillars (Hosea 10:1). The harvest was supposed to send them to the Giver, and instead they built shrines to the gifts. That's like getting a promotion and thanking the parking spot.

Then Hosea says they trusted in their own way and in the multitude of their mighty men (Hosea 10:13). Idols, fortresses, a king, big armies: all of it was a bunch of things that could not hold them up. Hosea says they plowed wickedness and reaped injustice (Hosea 10:13), because what you plant is what comes up. I think this part is heavy, and I think it's meant to be, because the LORD is not playing around with a heart that has gone devious.

But listen, because right in the middle of the hard news comes an invitation: “Sow for yourselves righteousness and reap the fruit of loving devotion; break up your unplowed ground.” (Hosea 10:12). It is time to seek the LORD until He comes and sends righteousness upon them like rain. So, baker, ask yourself what hard, unplowed ground is sitting in your life. Break it up and seek Him there, because that's where the rain falls.
